_comment: JPMorgan Chase Bank N.A. — FY2025 (year ended December 31, 2025)
_source: JPMorgan Chase 4Q25 Earnings Press Release, SEC Form 8-K FY2025, jpmorganchase.com
_note_balance_sheet: Total Assets $4,900.5B; Loans $1,526.4B (31.1% of assets — low vs Indian banks due to large IB/trading book); Deposits $2,675.5B (54.6%). LDR 57.1%. Cash & equivalents $1,582.2B (32%) due to Fed reserves and trading assets. World's largest bank by market cap.
_note_deposits: US banks have lower CASA ratios than Indian banks. Non-interest bearing demand ~25%, interest-bearing checking/savings ~42%, time deposits (CDs) ~33%. Large corporate/institutional deposit base.
_note_exposure: Consumer & Community Banking ~35% (mortgages 15%, auto/personal/cards 20%), Commercial Banking ~15% (middle market, CRE), Corporate & Investment Bank ~45% (large corporate, institutional), Asset/Wealth ~5%. Corporate-heavy due to dominant IB franchise.
_note_credit_quality: NPL ratio 0.66% — best-in-class among global banks. Allowance for loan losses 0.6% of total loans. Strong credit culture, diversified portfolio across US economic cycles.
_note_pnl: NIM 2.50% (down from 2.63% in FY2024 as Fed cut rates). Net income $55.7B. ROA 1.14%. ROE ~14.8%. Cost-income ~55%. Full year revenue $168.2B.
_note_capital: CET1 14.5%, Tier1 15.5%, Total Capital 17.4% (Standardized, Dec 2025). $288B CET1 capital. Well above Basel III minimums and US-specific GSIB surcharges.
